⏤ When sponsors aren’t available

TipJip still pays our Tippers.

When an ad slot has no sponsor lined up, TipJip fills it with a 15-second house ad — and pays the listener $0.10 out of our own pocket. We don’t charge a platform fee on house ads. Your attention is worth something even when a sponsor isn’t buying it, and the loop never goes cold.

Tippers — that’s what we call our verified listeners. Phone-verified, anonymous up to $600/year, and paid every time they choose to tip or jip an ad. See a Tipper account →

How it works

Listen.
Tip or jip.
Cash out.

Three steps. One episode. Between the podcaster, the listener, and the sponsor — no algorithms in the middle, no data brokers on the side.

01 — Listen

Up to 3 ad slots per episode.

Hit play. The host has chosen 1, 2, or 3 ad slots — and each is either a 30-second ad ($0.50 to your jar) or a 60-second host-read ($1.00). On Sally’s episode: pre-roll 30s, mid-stream 60s, post-roll 30s. $2.00 total, already yours. The sponsor pays you. 100% of the bid reaches your jar.

02 — Tip or jip

Their jar — or yours. Three times.

After each ad, you decide. Tip if the read landed — the coin goes to the podcaster with a thank-you. Jip if it didn't — the coin stays in your jar with anonymous feedback. Tap-tap-tap, three independent decisions per episode. The money flows. The data doesn't.

03 — Cash out

Empty the jar whenever.

Tips and jips both stack in your TipJip jar. Hit $15 and transfer to your bank or PayPal — no platform fees on cash-out, no waiting period after first verified payout. Or let it ride and tip the next podcaster. Your jar, your call.

Now multiply: 12,000 verified listeners × 92% blended tip rate gives roughly ~$22,000 in Sally's jar from this single episode. How we get paid

Advertisers pay us.
Nobody else.

One fee. Posted publicly. Same schedule for an indie supplement brand and a Fortune 500. No platform tax on viewers. No platform tax on creators.

TipJip earns one thing only: a platform fee charged to advertisers at checkout, on top of the listener payout — never deducted from the listener’s tip, never out of the creator’s earnings. Listeners see only the bid amount the advertiser pays them. Creators see only the tips listeners send. 100% of the bid reaches the listener.

Advertiser's bid → paid in full to the viewer
Matched delivery + 50% of bid · min $0.10 · max $0.50
Advertiser pays = bid plus matched delivery

The cap means premium advertisers pay a smaller effective rate as their bid grows — encouraging higher bids and richer audiences without runaway fees.

Pay the human for their attention. Not a proxy.

Every ad dollar you've spent for a decade went to a platform, an exchange, a data broker, a verification vendor, an attribution tool — and finally, a sliver, to the human who saw your ad. Privacy by architecture

Consent is the foundation.
Not the disclaimer.

Compliant with Washington's My Health My Data Act, California's CPRA, and every regulation coming next — built in from day one, not retrofitted under pressure.

"Privacy is the architecture, not a footer link. Every trait is opted in. Every share-out is logged. Every deletion propagates within 45 days. The audit trail isn't a feature — it's the product."

— TipJip Privacy Charter

  • Zero-party data only

    We never infer, scrape, or buy. If we know it, you told us.

  • One-click deletion

    One click. Removes your profile from us — and propagates to every advertiser who ever saw it.

  • HIPAA-aligned storage

    Health-adjacent traits encrypted at rest and in transit. Role-based access. Audit logs on every read.

  • Zero third-party tracking

    No pixels. No fingerprinting. No Google or Meta SDKs. We turned the surveillance graph off.

⏤ Step 2 of 3 · The one rule that matters

Real humans only.
That's the deal.

Before you create anything on TipJip, you agree to the platform's only non-negotiable rule. It's short. It's serious. And it's why advertisers and viewers trust us.

01
THE 100% REAL HUMAN RULE

The face on screen must be a real, consenting human. Yours.

No AI faces. No deepfakes. No synthetic performers. No voice cloning of yourself or anyone else. No face-swapping. No AI-generated patient testimonials. The human in your video must be the human who consented to be there.

You can use AI tools for editing, captions, music, supporting graphics, or B-roll — those just need to be disclosed in your video metadata. But the on-camera human is always real. Read the full standards →

⏤ Step 2 of 3 · Your NPI

Enter your
10-digit NPI.

Your National Provider Identifier — the same 10-digit number you use on insurance claims and prescription pads. We'll send it to the federal CMS NPPES registry to verify your credential is active and in good standing. Takes about 2 seconds.

10 digits, no dashes. Forgot your NPI? Look it up →
🔒
What we do with your NPI: Send it to npiregistry.cms.hhs.gov, receive your provider record, store the verified status (active/inactive) and credential letters on your TipJip account. We don't store your home address, SSN, or any data CMS doesn't already publish in the public registry.

⏤ NOT VERIFIED

We couldn't find that NPI
in the CMS registry.

The federal NPPES registry returned no active record for the number you entered. A few common reasons:

1 Typo in the 10-digit number — most common cause. Double-check.
2 Recently issued (last 7 days) — CMS takes a few days to publish new NPIs to the API.
3 Deactivated NPI — if your license has lapsed, the NPI is removed from the public registry until reinstated.
4 NPI is for an organization, not an individual — Type 2 NPIs aren't eligible. Use your Type 1 (individual provider) NPI.

⏤ Step 1 of 5 · Become an advertiser

Your ad spend goes
to humans.

Not to a data broker. Not to a bot farm. Not to a black-box auction. Every dollar you spend on TipJip lands directly in the jar of a phone-verified human who finished watching your ad. That's the entire ad model — no impressions, no estimated reach, no proxy metrics.

100%
VERIFIED HUMANS
Every viewer is phone-verified at signup. No bots, no MFA fraud, no SDK manipulation. The price is the price for a real person.
$0
FOR INCOMPLETE WATCHES
You only pay when a viewer completes the full watch with the slide-confirm UX. Mid-watch drop-offs cost you nothing. Best-in-class engagement guarantee.
$0.50–$3
DYNAMIC BID RANGE
You set your max bid per completed watch. Premium audiences (verified practitioners, podcast listeners) cost more. Standard reach is at the floor.
76%
AVG TIP RATE
The most honest engagement signal in advertising. Tip rate is the % of viewers who said "thanks for the ad" by tipping back. Higher than any survey.
THE 100% REAL HUMAN RULE APPLIES TO ADS TOO

Your ad creative must show real people or no people. No AI faces, no synthetic spokespeople, no deepfaked testimonials, no voice clones. You can use product shots, demos, motion graphics, music — but if there's a human in your ad, they are real and have consented. Read the full content rule →

Show analytics

Listens over time · Last 90 days

DROP-OFF POINT
Most listeners stop around 38 minutes.

About 22% of subscribers don't finish episodes longer than 60 minutes. Your mid-stream slot at 31:00 is hitting before this drop-off, which is why it converts well.

TOP TIPPED EPISODE
Episode 46 — "The myth of 8 hours"

81% tip rate. The framing — challenging conventional wisdom backed by data — got the most "thanks for the explanation" jip notes too. Pattern worth repeating.

JIP FEEDBACK THEME
"Felt like sponsor read"

3 jips this month called out mid-stream sponsor reads as feeling overscripted. Consider keeping the read in your voice but improvising more.

PROTOCOL v1.0 · TECHNICAL PREVIEW · MAY 2026

The TipJip Agent Protocol.
Honest by design.

An open spec defining how AI agents identify themselves when watching content on a human's behalf. Agents declare themselves, advertisers price accordingly, humans earn full bid for their own attention while agents earn at a reduced rate. The first formal protocol for the human/agent boundary in attention markets.

§1 · Overview §2 · Identification headers §3 · Watch payload schema §4 · Rate card §5 · Reference implementations §6 · Compliance notes
§1 · Overview

Why a protocol is needed.

By 2027, an estimated 30–40% of "viewers" on consumer platforms will be AI agents browsing on behalf of humans — researching products, watching demos, gathering information, drafting summaries. Most platforms will treat this as fraud and block it. That's the wrong move.

The right move is to formalize the distinction. Agents and humans both deliver value to advertisers — but different value. A human's emotional reaction, brand impression, and purchase intent flow from a human. An agent's information extraction, comparison, and downstream recommendation flow from a delegated process. Both are worth paying for. Neither should be priced as if it were the other.

The Agent Protocol formalizes this distinction so platforms, agents, and advertisers can interoperate without ambiguity. Honesty becomes the default state.

§2 · Identification headers

Required headers for agent traffic.

Any HTTP request originating from an AI agent acting on a human's behalf MUST set the following headers when interacting with TipJip surfaces:

X-TipJip-Actor: agent
X-TipJip-Agent-Vendor: "anthropic"          # lowercase, registered vendor slug
X-TipJip-Agent-Model: "claude-opus-4-7"     # model family / version
X-TipJip-On-Behalf-Of: "jar:4471"          # the human's jar number
X-TipJip-Task-Class: "research"             # research | summarize | shop | other
X-TipJip-Session-Id: "sess_a91kcbf"        # delegated session token

Missing or invalid headers result in the request being treated as unattested traffic, which earns no rate-card payout and is logged for audit. Vendors who fail to attest become subject to platform-level rate limiting.

§3 · Watch payload schema

What an agent watch looks like.

When an agent completes a watch event on behalf of a human, the platform receives a payload that distinguishes it from a human-attested watch:

{
  "event_type": "watch_complete",
  "actor": "agent",                    // human | agent
  "on_behalf_of": "jar:4471",
  "agent_attestation": {
    "vendor": "anthropic",
    "model": "claude-opus-4-7",
    "task_class": "research",
    "signature": "ed25519:a91k..."      // vendor-signed payload
  },
  "watch_proof": {
    "completion_pct": 1.0,
    "slide_confirmed": false,            // agents skip slide-to-confirm
    "agent_attention_signal": "transcript_extracted"
  },
  "rate_card_applied": "agent_research_30pct"
}
§4 · Rate card

Honest pricing per actor type.

Advertisers set their bid as before. The protocol applies a multiplier based on actor type and task class. Humans always earn 100% of bid. Agents earn a fraction reflecting the different value delivered. Platform fees are applied uniformly.

Actor Task class Multiplier of bid Notes
Human Direct watch (slide-confirmed) 100% Full bid, full attention proof.
Agent Research (info extraction) 30% Most common task class.
Agent Summarize (TL;DR) 25% No comparison, no decision support.
Agent Shop (recommend purchase) 50% Higher conversion intent justifies premium.
Agent Other / unattested 0% No payout. Logged for audit.

Multipliers are protocol-versioned and may be revised every 6 months based on observed conversion data. Vendors are notified 60 days before any change takes effect.

§5 · Reference implementations

Open-source SDK starters.

We've shipped reference implementations for the three most common agent runtimes. All are MIT-licensed and accept community contributions.

JS
tipjip-agent-node
github.com/tipjip/agent-node
PY
tipjip-agent-python
github.com/tipjip/agent-python
GO
tipjip-agent-go
github.com/tipjip/agent-go
§6 · Compliance notes

What this protocol is, and isn't.

The Agent Protocol is a commercial honesty standard, not a security mechanism. It assumes vendors who attest in good faith. Vendors who falsely attest (claiming human traffic for an agent, or vice versa) face platform-level deplatforming, vendor-slug revocation, and contractual liability.

The protocol does NOT:

— attempt to detect agents that don't self-attest (that's a hopeless arms race)
— prevent agents from operating (we welcome them)
— degrade the human experience in any way
— share agent attestations with advertisers without aggregation

The protocol DOES:

— give vendors who play honestly a clear commercial path
— give advertisers a clear pricing signal
— give humans full economic priority over their own attention
— give the entire industry a shared standard to converge on

⏤ For video podcasters

Health & wellness podcasters,
finally paid like creators.

Three ad slots. Your show, your rules. Pre-roll, mid-stream, post-roll — pick any combination. Verified human listeners pay you directly. No 50% platform tax. No ads from sketchy supplement brands. The first podcast platform built for the verified-human era.

01 · THE THREE-SLOT MODEL

You decide where the ads land.
Your show, your call.

Every slot you enable adds to the listener's tip jar. They tip you with thanks, or jip and keep it themselves with feedback. Three places to earn per episode. Or one. Whatever fits your show.

SLOT 1

Pre-roll

Before episode begins

Highest engagement, lowest skip. Ideal for shows where listeners commit to the full episode. Most podcasters enable this slot by default.

Listener earns$0.50–$3
Tip rate (current beta)82%
SLOT 2 · MOST VALUABLE

Mid-stream

You set the timestamp

Highest CPM in conventional podcasting ($30–$50). Listeners who reach mid-roll are committed. Use it once per episode, or skip it entirely for shows where flow matters more than ad inventory.

Listener earns$1–$5
Tip rate (current beta)76%
SLOT 3

Post-roll

After episode ends

Highest-intent inventory. Listeners who finish the episode are your committed audience. Cheaper per impression, but converts well for niche advertisers.

Listener earns$0.50–$2
Tip rate (current beta)88%
The mechanic, slightly different for podcasts: For a regular video, one ad runs and the listener immediately tips or jips. For a podcast, each enabled slot adds to the same jar. At episode end, your listener tips the whole jar to you, or jips and keeps it themselves with anonymous feedback. Three people, one transaction — just spread across an hour-long show.

⏤ Content Standards · The Rules

100% real humans.
No exceptions.

Every face you see on TipJip is a real person who chose to be there. Every voice belongs to a verified human. We don't allow synthetic performers, AI avatars, or deepfakes — at any percentage, in any format. This is the rule that defines what TipJip is.

01
THE 100% REAL HUMAN RULE

Every human face and voice on TipJip must belong to a real, consenting person.

AI-generated performers, synthetic avatars, deepfakes, voice clones, and AI-modified faces are not permitted under any circumstance. There is no acceptable percentage. There is no labeled-AI exception. Either the human in the video is real, or the video doesn't belong on TipJip.

02 · WHAT'S ALLOWED

The line we draw — and why.

AI tools have legitimate creative uses. We allow them where they support real human creators, and ban them where they replace real human creators. Here's exactly where the line sits.

✓ ALLOWED

AI as a creative tool

  • Editing & post-production. AI editing tools (cut detection, audio cleanup, color grading) are tools — like a camera or a microphone.
  • Supporting graphics & B-roll. AI-generated illustrations, animations, charts, or stock-style imagery used to illustrate concepts are fine, with metadata disclosure.
  • Captions, transcription, translation. Auto-generated captions and translation of the creator's actual spoken words are fine — and recommended for accessibility.
  • Background music. AI-composed music as background score is permitted with disclosure.
  • Research & scripting. Using AI to research topics or draft scripts is fine — the creator must read and own the content.
  • Thumbnails. AI-generated thumbnails are permitted with disclosure (note: must accurately represent video content).
✗ NOT ALLOWED

AI replacing the human

  • AI-generated faces. Synthetic performers, AI avatars, virtual influencers, generated headshots used as the on-camera presenter.
  • Deepfakes. Face-swap technology of any kind, including putting one human's face on another's body. Both are immediate suspension.
  • Voice cloning. AI-generated speech in the creator's voice — even of words the creator approves. The voice on the video must be the human speaking it.
  • AI-modified faces. Face-altering filters that shift age, ethnicity, or identity. (Cosmetic filters that smooth or color-correct are fine.)
  • Synthetic patient testimonials. AI-generated "patient" voices or faces describing experiences. Real patients only, with consent.
  • Lip-sync to AI voice. Real human face moving lips to AI-generated audio. Both must be real, both from the same person.
03 · WHY THIS RULE EXISTS

Other platforms got this wrong.
We learned from them.

38%

Of TikTok ad creatives in 2026 incorporate some form of AI-generated content. Labels exist, but most viewers don't notice them. Trust erodes invisibly.

89%

Of enterprise marketers said they won't work with AI avatars in 2026. Even the buy-side has lost confidence in synthetic content.

$5,000

Per-violation civil penalty under New York's S8420A for undisclosed synthetic performers in advertising. The legal direction is hardening fast.

The major platforms (YouTube, TikTok, Meta, X) tried to compromise: allow AI content if labeled. The result is a hybrid environment where labeled-AI sits next to real content, viewers can't tell the difference, and trust collapses for everyone. We chose the harder, simpler path: the rule. Bright line. No exceptions. Easy to enforce, easy to explain, easy to trust.

04 · HOW WE ENFORCE

The rule has teeth.

01

Identity verification at upload

Every creator account is tied to a verified human. For verified-practitioner tier, we cross-check professional licensing. The face on screen must match the face on file.

02

Automated detection on every video

C2PA metadata scanning, deepfake detection, voice biometric matching. Every uploaded video runs through detection before publish. Detection isn't perfect — but it sets the floor.

03

Viewer flagging

Every video has a "this looks fake" flag. Two flags from verified jars triggers a manual review within 24 hours. Verified humans are the strongest detection layer we have.

04

Suspension & clawback

Confirmed AI-generated humans = immediate account suspension and clawback of all earnings. Repeat or willful violations = permanent ban and the funds go to the affected viewers' jars.

05 · DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS

If you used AI for anything other than the human, label it.

Required AI-use disclosures in the video metadata. Failure to disclose is treated the same as a violation.

⏤ Company · About

Why we built TipJip.

Founder · TipJip

Randall Chesnutt

Entrepreneur. Best-selling author. Two decades of building things that pay creators back.

Spoken About Media · Founder O₂ Pro Academy · Founder

The short version

Randall has spent the last twenty years building businesses, brands, and platforms that put creators and customers in direct contact — without algorithms or data brokers in between. He’s a best-selling author (Open Your Mind and Let Doubt Out), a keynote speaker, the founder of three operating companies, and the kind of entrepreneur who launches a new venture when he sees a hole the rest of the industry refuses to fill.

TipJip is the hole he saw next.

The pattern across his work

Every business Randall has built sits at the same intersection: technology that respects the human on the other end.

  • Spoken About Media — a marketing and AI-services company that helps small businesses automate sales and content without selling out their customers’ data. Started in 2009; still operating today.
  • Ergo-Flex Technologies — the company behind Mito2™, the IHHT (intermittent hypoxic-hyperoxic) altitude therapy device used in 400+ clinics. Hardware, software, training, and certification — built for chiropractors and wellness practitioners, not Big Pharma.
  • O₂ Pro Academy — the certification arm. Certified Altitude Therapist (CAT) and Certified Regenerative Oxygen Specialist (CROS) are professional credentials Randall built from scratch because no one else was doing it right.
  • TipJip — the same instinct, applied to attention. Verified human listeners. Hosts who get paid by their audience instead of by algorithms. Advertisers who pay for human yeses instead of bot impressions.

Why podcasts

Randall has been on the podcast circuit for fifteen years — speaking, consulting, hosting, producing. He’s watched the same problem from every angle: the audience does the work, the platform takes the money, and the host barely covers their editor.

The math has gotten worse every year. Spotify takes its cut. YouTube takes its cut. The ad network takes its cut. Bots inflate the impressions. The data brokers sell off the listener’s preferences. The listener gets nothing — not even the dignity of being asked.

TipJip is the rebuild. Sponsors pay listeners directly. Listeners decide if the host earned it. The platform fee comes from advertisers, on top of what reaches the human — never deducted from the listener’s tip or the host’s earnings. 100% verified humans. 100% of the bid reaches the listener.

What he’s built before

Two decades of marketing and product strategy work, including teaching Facebook and Instagram advertising at industry events, building lead-generation systems for hundreds of small businesses, and developing AI-powered automation services that took small teams from zero to operational in weeks. He’s spoken to audiences from PodHouston to industry conferences across the country, and consulted with clinic owners, fitness brands, and direct-to-consumer companies on how to grow without losing the customer relationship.

The 10,000+ practitioner email list at Ergo-Flex, the 400+ clinics running Mito2™, and the working CAT/CROS certifications didn’t build themselves. They were built one phone call, one onboarding, one trust-earned conversation at a time. That’s the playbook for TipJip too.

The philosophy

“My personal and professional philosophy stems from my own shortcomings. Strive to understand thyself and respect those who are different. For those who are different just might have the answers you are seeking.”

— Randall Chesnutt

Randall lives in the greater Houston area. He’s a father, an author, and the kind of operator who would rather build the platform than complain about the one that exists. TipJip is what twenty years of pattern-recognition decided to build next.

⏤ Standards & legal · Privacy

Privacy Charter.

Privacy is the architecture of TipJip, not a footer link. Every trait you share is opted in. Every share-out is logged. Every deletion propagates within 45 days. The audit trail isn’t a feature — it’s the product.

Note: This is a plain-English summary of how TipJip handles personal information. A full legal Privacy Policy will replace this page at public launch and will incorporate the obligations and definitions required under GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and state-level U.S. privacy laws. For the private beta, this Charter is binding on TipJip operationally; any conflict between this Charter and the eventual Privacy Policy will be resolved in your favor.

What we collect · and only this

  • Phone number — required for human verification. Stored hashed and encrypted at rest. Never shared with advertisers, podcasters, or third parties.
  • Email (optional) — for receipts, cash-out confirmations, and account recovery only. Never shared.
  • Self-declared interests (e.g., “hormone health,” “longevity”) — only what you explicitly toggle on. Visible to advertisers only as a targeting category, never tied to your phone number or identity.
  • Self-declared demographics (age range, region) — broad buckets only. We never store city, ZIP, or exact location.
  • Listening logs — which episodes you played and your tip/jip decisions. Used by the platform to compute your jar balance and the podcaster’s earnings. Not shared with anyone, including the podcaster, beyond the aggregate stats they need to operate.
  • Bank account or PayPal details — only when you cash out. Handled by Stripe Connect; TipJip never stores your bank credentials directly.
  • Real name + SSN (W-9) — only once your jar earns more than $600 in a calendar year, as required by U.S. tax law for 1099-NEC issuance. Used for tax reporting; never shared with advertisers or podcasters.

What we never collect

  • Your name (until the $600/year tax threshold is crossed).
  • Your physical address (ever, except as required for tax forms).
  • Your browsing history outside of TipJip.
  • Cross-site tracking pixels, third-party cookies, advertising IDs.
  • Biometric data beyond the optional voice sample for instant cash-out, which is hashed and stored only for verification matching.

What we never sell or share

TipJip does not sell your data. We do not share data with data brokers. We do not let advertisers retarget you off-platform. The platform fee on advertisers is the only revenue model — we make money when sponsors pay you, period.

Your rights

  • Export your data — full machine-readable export of everything we have on your jar, on request, within 7 days.
  • Delete your data — full deletion within 45 days of request, with the legally required exceptions for transaction records and tax forms (which must be retained for 7 years per IRS rules).
  • Pause your jar — stop receiving sponsored ads at any time, without deleting your account.
  • See every share-out — every time advertiser categories matched your jar, the audit log records it. You can review it in your Profile.

Security

Payment processing is handled by Stripe (PCI DSS Level 1). Phone verification by Twilio. Database hosted in U.S. regions with at-rest encryption. Access to production data is restricted to a single founder during private beta; expanded with audit logging at public launch. We will publish a security disclosure policy and bug bounty before scaling past 1,000 active Tippers.

Children

TipJip is intended for users 18 and older. We do not knowingly collect data from users under 18. Phone verification requires the user to confirm age 18+ at signup.

⏤ Standards & legal · Terms

Terms of Service.

Plain-English terms for the TipJip private beta. These will be replaced by a full, attorney-drafted Terms of Service before public launch. For the private beta, this version is the binding agreement between you (whether a Tipper, podcaster, or advertiser) and TipJip, Inc.

Plain-English summary: Don’t commit fraud. Pay what you owe. We’ll pay what we owe. We can suspend bad actors. You can leave any time. Disputes are resolved by good-faith mediation first, then by arbitration. We’re building something new; help us not break it.

1. Definitions

  • TipJip — the platform operated by TipJip, Inc., a [Delaware C-Corporation] based in [Houston, TX].
  • Tipper — a phone-verified individual listener with a TipJip jar account.
  • Podcaster — a content creator who has been approved to host episodes with TipJip ad slots.
  • Advertiser — a legal entity that has been approved to fund campaigns on TipJip.
  • Bid — the amount an Advertiser commits per Tipper exposure for one ad slot ($0.50 minimum for 30-second slots, $1.00 minimum for 60-second slots).
  • Tip — the Tipper’s decision to send their slot earnings to the Podcaster.
  • Jip — the Tipper’s decision to keep their slot earnings in their own jar, optionally with feedback.

2. Account eligibility

  • All users must be 18 years of age or older.
  • Tipper accounts require a verifiable U.S. phone number (VOIP numbers not accepted at signup).
  • Podcaster and Advertiser accounts require a verified legal entity and Stripe Connect onboarding (which includes KYC).
  • One Tipper account per verified phone number, per device, enforced at signup.

3. Listener (Tipper) terms

By creating a Tipper account, you agree to:

  • Use only one account, tied to a real phone number you control.
  • Not run multiple episodes simultaneously, not use bots or scripts, not artificially inflate your earnings, and not collude with podcasters or advertisers to manipulate tip rates.
  • Comply with daily and per-window consumption limits (currently 12 episodes/day, 36 decisions/day, 3 episodes per 4-hour window). Limits may be adjusted; you will be notified in-app.
  • Wait through any first-cash-out hold period (currently 7 days) and respond to any KYC requests at the $600/year W-9 threshold.
  • Accept that flagged accounts may be suspended pending review and that fraudulent activity will result in account termination and forfeiture of any unpaid balance.

4. Podcaster terms

By creating a Podcaster account, you agree to:

  • Submit truthful information about your show, listener counts, and audience demographics.
  • Read sponsor scripts as approved or request edits before approval. Do not modify scripts after final approval without re-submitting.
  • Comply with TipJip’s content standards: no AI-generated content, no false claims (especially health-related), no content that violates TipJip’s prohibited-content list.
  • Accept that TipJip may pause your show or suspend your account if your content is found to violate standards or applicable law.
  • Understand that platform-fee charges to advertisers are separate from your earnings; 100% of every tip a listener sends you reaches you, minus only the Stripe payment-processing cost on cash-out (currently absorbed by TipJip during private beta).

5. Advertiser terms

By creating an Advertiser account, you agree to:

  • Pre-fund your campaign budget via Stripe. Funds remain in your account balance until consumed by listener exposures.
  • Pay the listener payout ($0.50 for 30s, $1.00 for 60s minimum) plus a 25% TipJip platform fee on top.
  • Submit accurate creative scripts. False claims, prohibited products (firearms, illegal substances, predatory financial products, MLM), or content that violates TipJip’s policies will be rejected.
  • Accept that listener jip rates and feedback are not refundable. Listeners choosing to jip is the engagement signal; you pay only for tipped exposures plus the platform fee.
  • Not attempt to identify, contact, or retarget individual Tippers off-platform.

6. Payments & refunds

  • Tipper cash-out minimum: $15. First cash-out subject to 7-day hold; subsequent cash-outs typically same-day via Stripe.
  • Podcaster payouts: weekly, all tips received in the prior week, paid via Stripe Connect.
  • Advertiser refunds: unspent campaign balance is refundable at any time. Spent budget (paid to listeners) is not refundable except in cases of documented platform fraud (e.g., collusion ring detection).
  • Chargebacks: Advertiser chargebacks must be filed within 14 days. Disputed charges that are upheld will result in account suspension pending review.

7. Suspension and termination

TipJip may suspend or terminate any account at any time for: fraud, violation of these Terms, violation of content standards, threats to platform integrity, or as required by law. Suspended accounts will receive notice and the opportunity to appeal except in cases of clear fraud. Voluntary account closure is supported at any time via the in-app deletion flow.

8. Disputes

Any dispute will be resolved first via good-faith email mediation with TipJip support. If unresolved within 30 days, disputes are subject to binding arbitration under [JAMS Streamlined Arbitration Rules], seated in [Houston, Texas]. Class-action waivers apply.

9. Limitation of liability

TipJip’s liability to any user is limited to the lesser of (a) $500 or (b) the total platform fees paid by that user in the 12 months preceding the claim. TipJip is not liable for indirect, consequential, or punitive damages. Some jurisdictions do not allow these limitations; in those, our liability is limited to the maximum extent permitted.

10. Changes

We may update these Terms. Material changes will be communicated via email and in-app notice at least 14 days before taking effect. Continued use after the effective date constitutes acceptance.

⏤ Standards & legal · Cookies

Cookie Policy.

TipJip uses cookies and similar technologies sparingly — only what’s needed to keep you signed in, protect against fraud, and remember your preferences. We do not use cookies for cross-site tracking, behavioral advertising, or third-party analytics.

What we use

  • Essential cookies — session token (keeps you signed in), CSRF token (prevents form forgery), and a small set of preferences (theme, language). These cannot be disabled because the platform won’t function without them.
  • Fraud-prevention fingerprint — we use FingerprintJS to detect when many accounts use the same device. The fingerprint is stored as a hashed identifier, not linked to any personally identifiable information off-platform.
  • localStorage — for the demo pages on this site, we use localStorage to remember your sample-account state. This stays entirely on your device and is never sent to TipJip’s servers.

What we don’t use

  • Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, Twitter Pixel, LinkedIn Insight Tag, or any other ad-tech tracker.
  • Third-party advertising cookies. Sponsors targeting Tippers do so via opted-in trait categories, not cross-site tracking.
  • Cross-site session sharing with O₂ Pro Academy, Ergo-Flex, or any other Randall Chesnutt company.

How to control cookies

Most browsers allow you to block or delete cookies via Settings > Privacy. Note that blocking essential cookies will sign you out of TipJip and prevent core functions. We will add a cookie consent banner in compliance with GDPR/CCPA before public launch.

Updates

If we add a new cookie or tracking technology, this page will be updated and you will be notified in-app.

⏤ Standards & legal · Sponsorship

Sponsorship Policy.

TipJip exists to put sponsor dollars directly into the hands of verified humans. We are protective of who those sponsors are and what they say.

Who can advertise

Sponsors must be verified legal entities with a real product or service. We verify by:

  • Confirming corporate registration (LLC, Corp, or international equivalent).
  • Reviewing the advertiser’s website, product, and any prior consumer complaints or legal actions.
  • Confirming a verified business payment method via Stripe.

Prohibited categories

The following are not permitted as TipJip sponsors:

  • Firearms, ammunition, and weapons accessories.
  • Illegal substances, recreational drugs, and any unapproved pharmaceutical claims.
  • Predatory financial products: payday loans, get-rich-quick schemes, MLM/network-marketing, unregistered securities.
  • Gambling, sports betting, and online casinos (unless licensed in the listener’s state and verified by TipJip).
  • Adult content, escort services, and any sexually explicit material.
  • Health products making unapproved disease claims (e.g., “cures cancer,” “reverses diabetes”).
  • Political campaigns, advocacy organizations, and election-related advertising.
  • Tobacco, vapes, and nicotine products.

Script and content review

Every sponsor read on TipJip goes through three checkpoints:

  • 1. Sponsor submission — the advertiser writes the proposed read.
  • 2. Podcaster review — the host approves, requests edits, or rejects.
  • 3. TipJip final review — the platform flags scripts containing prohibited claims (medical, financial, “guaranteed,” etc.) and requires resolution before the slot can serve.

Earnings claims (FTC compliance)

Sponsors may not make earnings claims in their reads about TipJip itself, about the host’s income, or about listener Tipper earnings. Such claims are subject to FTC Business Opportunity Rule (16 CFR §437) and require substantiation we don’t have during the private beta period. Earnings figures on TipJip’s own marketing pages are illustrative and clearly labeled.

Sponsor suspension

Sponsors may be suspended for: false claims, repeated rejected scripts, attempting to retarget Tippers off-platform, attempting to identify individual Tippers, manipulating tip rates via collusion, or any prohibited-category activity discovered after onboarding.

⏤ Standards & legal · Health Data

Health Data Policy.

TipJip operates in wellness, longevity, hormone health, and metabolic categories. Many Tippers share interests that, in other contexts, would be considered sensitive health information. We hold ourselves to a higher standard than the law requires.

What we treat as health data

  • Self-declared interest categories that touch on health (hormone health, metabolic, sleep, longevity, supplements, etc.).
  • Information voluntarily shared in jip notes that may reference health conditions, treatments, or providers.
  • Any listener-declared lifestyle attributes (diet, fitness, sleep priority) that could be inferred as health-related.

How we protect it

  • Aggregate only — when sponsors target by interest category, they see audience size and tip rate at the category level. They never see individual Tipper profiles.
  • Never linked to identity — interest categories are stored linked only to your jar number, never to your phone, name, or email.
  • Never sold or shared with health data brokers — not to insurance companies, not to pharmaceutical marketers, not to data aggregators.
  • Jip notes are private by default — visible to the recipient podcaster only, never aggregated or sold.

HIPAA

TipJip is not a covered entity or business associate under HIPAA. We do not process Protected Health Information (PHI) as defined under HIPAA. Tipper-declared interests are not PHI — they are voluntary marketing preferences, comparable to a magazine subscription category. If you are a healthcare provider considering using TipJip to promote services, contact us before signup.

No medical advice

Nothing on TipJip — including episode content, sponsor reads, or platform copy — constitutes medical advice. Podcasters and sponsors making health-related claims do so on their own responsibility, subject to TipJip’s Sponsorship Policy and applicable FTC and FDA regulations.

Reporting concerns

If you believe a podcaster or sponsor on TipJip is making health claims that may harm listeners, please report it: trust@tipjip.com. Concerns will be reviewed within 48 hours.
